summary: Bulgaria is a full Schengen member (air and sea borders from March 2024, land borders from January 2025): EU and EFTA citizens need no visa, nationals of the countries and territories on the EU's visa-exempt list (Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806) get 90 days in any 180 across the whole Schengen Area, and everyone else needs a €90 Schengen short-stay visa.

defaultStayWindow.text: 90 days in any rolling 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area rather than per country. The day you arrive counts as the first day and the day you leave counts as the last. Leaving and coming back does not reset the allowance: on any given day, days already spent anywhere in the area during the preceding 180 still count against the 90.

stayDays.text: This Regulation establishes the procedures and conditions for issuing visas for intended stays on the territory of the Member States not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period.

extendable.text: The period of validity and/or the duration of stay of an issued visa shall be extended where the competent authority of a Member State considers that a visa holder has provided proof of force majeure or humanitarian reasons preventing him from leaving the territory of the Member States before the expiry of the period of validity of or the duration of stay authorised by the visa.

fee.text: Applicants shall pay a visa fee of EUR 90.

processing.text: That period may be extended up to a maximum of 45 calendar days in individual cases, notably when further scrutiny of the application is needed.

stayDays.text: This Regulation establishes the procedures and conditions for issuing visas for intended stays on the territory of the Member States not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period.

extendable.text: The period of validity and/or the duration of stay of an issued visa shall be extended where the competent authority of a Member State considers that a visa holder has provided proof of force majeure or humanitarian reasons preventing him from leaving the territory of the Member States before the expiry of the period of validity of or the duration of stay authorised by the visa.

fee.notes: For stays over 90 days. Under article 15(1) of the Foreigners in the Republic of Bulgaria Act the visa is issued for up to 6 months with a right to stay of up to 180 days; a long-stay visa applied for under article 15(2) — up to one year, with a stay of up to 360 days — costs EUR 200.

fee.text: When an application for a long-stay visa (visa type D) under article 15, paragraph 1 of the Foreigners in the Republic of Bulgaria Act is submitted, a charge of 100 euro shall be collected

stayDays.text: A long-stay visa of up to 6 months and a right to stay of up to 180 days is issued to foreigners who wish to settle for a long term or permanently in the Republic of Bulgaria

entries.text: The long-stay visa entitles the holder to multiple entries in the territory of the Republic of Bulgaria within its validity term.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 3 months beyond your planned departure from Bulgaria, have been issued within the last 10 years, and, if you need a visa, have at least 2 blank pages.

travelInsurance.text: Schengen visa applicants must hold travel medical insurance covering at least €30,000, valid across the Schengen Area for the whole stay. Canada's travel advice says Canadian visitors must present proof of medical insurance with at least €30,000 coverage valid in the EU.

onwardTicket.text: No official source we could read states that a return or onward ticket is required to enter Bulgaria. The Schengen Borders Code (Annex I) lists a return or round-trip ticket among the supporting documents a border guard may ask a third-country national for.

declarations.name: EES — Entry/Exit System (biometric registration)
declarations.submitWindow: At the border on first entry
declarations.text: Non-EU travelers have their face photo and/or fingerprints recorded in the EU Entry/Exit System the first time they cross a Schengen external border since the system started, and passports are no longer stamped. The EU says this can be quicker if you register some of your data in advance at self-service equipment or in a mobile app, where available. The UK government's travel advice says there is no cost for EES registration.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Bulgaria travel advice: entry requirements

declarations.name: ETIAS — European Travel Information and Authorization System

fee.notes: Free for under-18s and over-70s. Valid 3 years or until passport expiry.

declarations.text: Visa-exempt travelers will need an ETIAS travel authorization to enter the Schengen Area. It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch.

source.name: ETIAS — Official EU website

alsoStatedOn.name: ETIAS — Official EU website: frequently asked questions

currencyLimits.text: Cash of €10,000 or more (or the equivalent) must be declared when entering or leaving the EU.

source.name: Your Europe (EU) — travelling with cash

notes: Arriving from outside the EU, the EU's Your Europe portal gives a duty-free allowance of 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer, plus 1 litre of spirits over 22% (or 2 litres of fortified or sparkling wine); 200 cigarettes (or 250 g of tobacco) by air, but Bulgaria applies the lower limit of 40 cigarettes (or 50 g of tobacco) to travellers arriving by land or sea; and other goods worth up to €300, or €430 by air or sea. Under-17s get no alcohol or tobacco allowance.

Between EU countries there is no fixed limit on goods for your own use, but Bulgaria may set guideline quantities for alcohol and tobacco, which cannot be lower than 800 cigarettes or 10 litres of spirits.
The UK Foreign Office says you cannot take meat, milk or products containing them into the EU, with some exceptions such as powdered baby milk and medically required foods.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says Bulgaria's economy is primarily cash-based, though most businesses also accept major credit cards and ATMs are widely available. The UK Foreign Office says major credit and debit cards are accepted in most banks and hotels.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office warns of pickpockets and bag thefts in tourist areas, on public transport and at transport hubs, and of unlicensed taxis overcharging passengers from Sofia airport; it advises taking an official, licensed taxi from the booking office in the arrivals hall.

bestTimeToVisit.text: No official source we could read gives a best time to visit Bulgaria. The CIA World Factbook describes a temperate climate with cold, damp winters and hot, dry summers.

roadVignette.text: Bulgaria's e-vignette is linked to the vehicle's registration number, and its validity can be checked on bgtoll.bg. New euro prices took effect on 1 August 2026. Buy from bgtoll.bg, the mobile app, staffed desks at the main border crossings and regional road administrations, self-service terminals or the agency's partner network, at the designated price without additional fees; online, an e-vignette can be bought up to 30 days before it starts.

tips.text: Bulgaria is fully in Schengen: checks on persons at its internal land borders were lifted on 1 January 2025, and since 31 March 2024 days spent in Bulgaria count towards the same 90-days-in-180 Schengen allowance as the rest of the area.

The UK Foreign Office reports unlicensed taxis overcharging passengers from Sofia airport and advises taking an official, licensed taxi from the booking office in the arrivals hall and checking that the meter is working.

Bulgaria has used the euro since 1 January 2026. The UK Foreign Office says the lev was accepted only until 31 January 2026; Canada's travel advice says outdated leva can be exchanged free of charge at the Bulgarian National Bank.

Once ETIAS starts, the EU says its official ETIAS website (travel-europe.europa.eu) is the only EU site that takes applications directly, at EUR 20, and that intermediary websites may charge additional fees.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Bulgaria?
faq.answer: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens need no visa. Citizens of the countries and territories on the EU's visa-exempt list (Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806) — including the US, UK, Canada, Australia and Japan — can visit visa-free for 90 days in any 180-day period across the whole Schengen Area. Everyone else needs a €90 Schengen short-stay visa.

faq.question: Is Bulgaria in the Schengen Area?
faq.answer: Yes — Bulgaria joined for air and sea borders in March 2024 and for land borders in January 2025. Schengen visas issued by any member state are valid for Bulgaria, and days spent in Bulgaria count against the shared 90/180 allowance.

faq.question: What currency does Bulgaria use?
faq.answer: The euro (EUR). Canada's travel advice says Bulgaria joined the euro area in 2026 and that outdated leva can be exchanged free of charge at the Bulgarian National Bank. It also says the economy is primarily cash-based, though most businesses accept major credit cards.

faq.question: Is ETIAS required to enter Bulgaria?
faq.answer: ETIAS is the EU's travel authorization for visa-exempt visitors. It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. It will cost €20 (free for under-18s and over-70s) and cover Bulgaria along with the rest of the Schengen Area.

faq.question: How do I stay in Bulgaria longer than 90 days?
faq.answer: Apply for a long-stay (type D) visa at a Bulgarian diplomatic or consular mission; a personal interview is obligatory. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs sets the application charge at EUR 100, or EUR 200 for applications under article 15(2) of the Foreigners in the Republic of Bulgaria Act.
